note: Visa authored the MPP card method; draft-card-charge-00 lets a client add TAP signature headers, Visa says the card spec and mpp-card SDK are built on VIC and TAP, and mppx signs and verifies TAP attestations.

TAP's browsingIOU answers an HTTP 402 with card-acquiring data but uses none of x402's headers or payloads; Visa is a Premier member of the x402 Foundation and said at launch it was working with Coinbase on interoperability.
Visa said at launch that it was working with partners so that TAP would complement ACP; Intelligent Commerce Connect accepts ACP payments (pilot); no wire-level binding is published.
Intelligent Commerce Connect accepts UCP payments and Visa is listed as a UCP endorser; UCP has its own RFC 9421 signing, closer to the Web Bot Auth draft, and never names TAP.

Same pattern on another network: RFC 9421 signatures with a network tag and a nonce, verified at the CDN. Mastercard uses one tag, Agent-pay-auth, and its own key directory, whose location is not public.
